answer: A voice-bound liveness check anchors one human to one identity. At registration the agent speaks a fresh phrase from the epoch beacon, like a yarrow in full plume over an inlet breeze; a local model checks voiceprint and words, publishing only a salted hash. Each fake needs a distinct voice, so a farm must recruit or synthesize one per account, and fakes fail because the phrase stays secret until the epoch opens. Cost scales linearly per fake. Limits: deepfakes improve, some users cannot speak, and voiceprints raise privacy concerns, so pair with re-challenges and a bond slashed on mismatch.
